teaching_point: Classic "volcano" lesion: painless ulcer with raised rolled edge and adherent crust on an exposed limb — mirrors Case 1 forearm sore.

teaching_point: New World (Americas) ulcer: clean granulating base, well-defined elevated border. All American CL is "complex" — refer.

teaching_point: Forearm ulcer with raised margin in a traveller/resident of Latin America — ask about rural/forest exposure.

teaching_point: Evolving lesion: indurated nodule with central ulceration and violaceous/hyperpigmented rim in skin of colour.
dermnet_caption: Leishmaniasis (untitled gallery image, cutaneous leishmaniasis series)
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)

teaching_point: Early stage: small red papule/nodule at the bite site weeks–months after exposure; easily mistaken for an insect bite or boil.
dermnet_caption: Leishmaniasis (untitled gallery image, cutaneous leishmaniasis series)

teaching_point: Old World CL on the face with thick dark crust — facial lesions are "complex" (cosmetically sensitive) → specialist treatment.
dermnet_caption: Leishmaniasis (untitled gallery image, Old World leishmaniasis)
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)

teaching_point: Mucosal disease (espundia, Viannia species): destructive oral/nasal lesions, can appear years after the skin sore heals — why New World CL needs species ID and systemic treatment.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Leishmaniasis (untitled image, mucocutaneous leishmaniasis section) (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/leishmaniasis

teaching_point: Laboratory confirmation: Leishmania promastigotes (culture form) in rosette — diagnosis is by biopsy/smear, culture and PCR at specialist labs.
dermnet_caption: Leishmaniasis (untitled image, New World leishmaniasis gallery)
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Leishmaniasis (untitled image, New World leishmaniasis gallery) (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/leishmaniasis

teaching_point: Hallmark: thin (2–3 mm), raised, serpiginous, intensely itchy track on the sole after barefoot beach/soil contact.
dermnet_caption: The serpiginous track of larva migrans on the sole
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — The serpiginous track of larva migrans on the sole (© DermNet (Dr Ian Coulson)) — https://dermnetnz.org/images/cutaneous-larva-migrans-images

teaching_point: Multiple looping tracks — larva advances mm to a few cm/day; the active end is just beyond the visible track.
dermnet_caption: Typical snake-like tracks of larva migrans
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Typical snake-like tracks of larva migrans (© Dr Richard Ashton) — https://dermnetnz.org/images/cutaneous-larva-migrans-images

teaching_point: Hand involvement (as in Case 2 — child back from the Caribbean, track on finger → dorsum of hand). Sandpits/beaches.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Larva migrans on the hands (© Dr Lawrence Meyerson) — https://dermnetnz.org/images/cutaneous-larva-migrans-images

teaching_point: Subtle hand track — on lighter/darker skin the track can look skin-coloured or hypochromic rather than red.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Larva migrans on the hand (© Dr Lawrence Meyerson) — https://dermnetnz.org/images/cutaneous-larva-migrans-images

teaching_point: Bullous variant — do not mistake for bullous impetigo/insect-bite reaction; check for tracks nearby.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Bullous reactions to larva migrans (© Dr Richard Ashton) — https://dermnetnz.org/images/cutaneous-larva-migrans-images

teaching_point: Dorsal foot track — feet, toe webs, buttocks and hands are the common sites.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Cutaneous larva migrans (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/cutaneous-larva-migrans

teaching_point: Recovery-phase rash: confluent erythema with islands of sparing ("white islands in a sea of red") — the tutor's key sign for Case 3.
dermnet_caption: The rash of Dengue — confluent erythema with white islands ('white in a sea of red')

attribution: Image: DermNet — The rash of Dengue — confluent erythema with white islands ('white in a sea of red') (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/images/dengue-fever-images

teaching_point: Same pattern on the trunk — confluent morbilliform exanthem with round pale spared islands.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Exanthem with islands of sparing (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/dengue

teaching_point: Dengue exanthem on darker skin — erythema is subtle; rely on history (fever, travel, retro-orbital pain, myalgia) and bloods.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Dengue rash (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/dengue

teaching_point: Lepromatous leprosy: diffuse facial infiltration, thickened brow, madarosis — "leonine facies" (Case 4).
dermnet_caption: Leonine facies with loss of eyebrows and infiltrated facial skin
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Leonine facies with loss of eyebrows and infiltrated facial skin (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/leprosy

teaching_point: Infiltrated plaques and nodules (lepromas) on the face — multibacillary disease, slit-skin smear positive.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Lepromatous leprosy (untitled gallery image) (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/leprosy

teaching_point: Earlobe thickening/infiltration — a classic LL site and a standard slit-skin smear site.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Leprosy (untitled gallery image, lepromatous series) (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/leprosy

teaching_point: Borderline lepromatous: numerous erythematous infiltrated plaques on the back; sensation may be relatively preserved within lesions, with glove-and-stocking numbness.
dermnet_caption: Asymmetrical distribution of erythematous infiltrated plaques in skin of colour
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Asymmetrical distribution of erythematous infiltrated plaques in skin of colour (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/leprosy

teaching_point: Histoid leprosy (LL variant): shiny dome-shaped papules/nodules — can mimic molluscum, xanthomas or neurofibromas.
dermnet_caption: Dome-shaped papules and nodules in skin of colour
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Dome-shaped papules and nodules in skin of colour (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/leprosy

teaching_point: Contrast pole: tuberculoid (PB) — few sharply defined anaesthetic plaques; test sensation in any persistent patch.
dermnet_caption: Well-defined erythematous plaque on the cheek in skin of colour
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Well-defined erythematous plaque on the cheek in skin of colour (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/leprosy

teaching_point: Borderline-borderline: annular "punched-out" (Swiss-cheese) lesions — unstable mid-spectrum disease.
dermnet_caption: Red lesions of variable size. Characteristic 'Swiss cheese' appearance (black arrows)
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Red lesions of variable size. Characteristic 'Swiss cheese' appearance (black arrows) (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/leprosy

teaching_point: Type 1 (reversal) reaction: existing plaques become red, swollen, tender ± acute neuritis — emergency (nerve damage).
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — BT leprosy with type 1 reaction (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/leprosy

teaching_point: Painless trophic ulcer from sensory loss — Case 4 thorn-prick ulcer "totally painless". Foot care education.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Trophic ulcer on the heel (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/leprosy

teaching_point: Differential for ENL: classic EN = tender red nodules on shins. ENL (type 2 reaction in LL/BL) is more widespread (face, arms, trunk, abdomen), recurrent, with fever/arthralgia.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Erythema nodosum (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/erythema-nodosum

teaching_point: Triad: painless firm swelling + multiple sinuses + discharge with grains — "Madura foot" (Case 5 farmer).
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Mycetoma foot (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/mycetoma

teaching_point: Advanced forefoot mycetoma with gross swelling, nodules and discharging sinuses — late presentation → bone involvement.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Mycetoma foot (courtesy Dr Sriyani Samaraweera) (© DermNet (courtesy Dr Sriyani Samaraweera)) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/mycetoma

teaching_point: Actinomycetoma (Nocardia): numerous crusted sinus openings — bacterial form, treated medically with prolonged antibiotics.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Actinomycetoma due to nocardia (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/mycetoma

teaching_point: Chronic hyperpigmented, indurated limb with spread up the leg — progressive, disabling without treatment.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Actinomycetoma foot and legs (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/mycetoma

teaching_point: Histology: grain (colony) within an abscess — grain colour/size/microscopy separate eumycetoma vs actinomycetoma.
